'''Lalchand Hirachand Doshi''' (24 October 1904 – 1993)  was a scion of [[Walchand group]], noted industrialist, [[Philanthropy|philanthropist]] and [[Jain]] social leader.<ref name=a>[http://premier.co.in/we/corporate/premier-legacy/308-premier-legacy-lalchand.html Lalchand Hirachand] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120203045120/http://premier.co.in/we/corporate/premier-legacy/308-premier-legacy-lalchand.html |date=2012-02-03 }}</ref><ref name=b/>

He was the youngest son of Hirachand Doshi from his second marriage and was half-brother of [[Walchand Hirachand]], who was born from first marriage of his father. He was born in [[Solapur]] Maharashtra into a [[Jain]] family.<ref name=x>[https://books.google.com/books?id=dm0AAAAAMAAJ&q=gulabchand+hirachand+died Progressive Jains of India – Satish Kumar Jain – Google Books<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=Gt5WXOQ08DYC&dq=gulabchand+hirachand+%28born+-died%29&pg=PA639 Business Legends – Gita Piramal – Google Books<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> Name of his other brothers were [[Gulabchand Hirachand]] and [[Ratanchand Hirachand]].<ref name=x/>

He completed his Bachelor of Arts degree from [[Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute|Deccan College, Pune]]. He was admitted to the [[Middle Temple]] in London on 12 November 1926,<ref>Sturgess, H.A.C. (1949). ''Register of Admissions to the Honourable Society of the Middle Temple''. Butterworth & Co. (Publishers) Ltd.: Temple Bar. Vol. 3, p.895.</ref> but withdrew without being [[Called to the Bar]] on 8 November 1928. He married Lalitabai in June 1931, with whom he had three sons and a daughter.<ref name=b/>

When he grew up he joined his brother, Walchand and served its various group companies including [[The Scindia Steam Navigation Company Ltd.]], [[Walchandnagar Industries]], [[Hindustan Aeronautics Limited]], Ravalgaon Sugar, [[Hindustan Construction Company]], and [[Premier Automobiles Limited]].<ref name=x/> He later served also as president of the [[Indian Merchants' Chamber]] and various other merchant bodies.<ref name=a/>

He also served as president of All India [[Digambara|Digamber Jain]] Tirthakshetra Committee from 1972 to 1983, and was connected to a number of charitable institutions.<ref name=b/> He is also the author an acclaimed  book on [[Ramayana]] named as ''The Indian epic – Ramayana''.<ref name=b>[http://jainsamaj.org/rpg_site/literature2.php?id=991&cat=62 Jain Samaj – Seth Lalchand Hirachand]</ref>

He was elected as an independent candidate as member of the [[Bombay Legislative Council]], in 1939.<ref name=a/><ref>{{cite book|title=Indian Business and Nationalist Politics 1931–39: The Indigenous Capitalist ... By Claude Markovits|year=2002|pages=123|isbn=9780521016827|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=b-URirZAjjQC&q=lalchand+hirachand&pg=PA123|last1=Markovits|first1=Claude|publisher=Cambridge University Press }}</ref>  After [[Indian independence movement|India's independence]], he also became a member of the [[Rajya Sabha]] from 1952 to 1958.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.indianautographs.com/productdetail-119123.html |title=Lalchand Hirachand Doshi – Member of Rajya Sabha – 1952–58 |access-date=28 August 2012 |archive-date=3 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211003064428/http://www.indianautographs.com/productdetail-119123.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was elected as the president of the Mechanical Engineers Association (India), Bombay for 1964–65 Session.{{cn|date=September 2017}}

A sports aficionado, he was a member of the [[Cricket Club of India]], the [[Willingdon Sports Club]] and various similar institutions. In addition, he was an avid golfer. He won the Dunlop Trophy for Golf and enjoyed playing tennis, badminton and bridge. He held a commercial pilot's license.<ref>{{cite web|title=Legacy|url=http://www.premier.co.in/legacy.html|accessdate=6 October 2014|archive-date=7 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141007034611/http://www.premier.co.in/legacy.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He died in October, 1993.<ref name=b/> Walchandnagar Industries is now run his sons Vinod Doshi, Chakor L. Doshi and others, whereas other companies went to sons of Gulabchand Hirachand, after family division of businesses, as the founder of the group Walchand Hirachand died without any male heirs.<ref>[http://www.walchand.com/board%20of%20directors.htm Walchandnagar Industries Limited] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120815124805/http://www.walchand.com/board%20of%20directors.htm |date=2012-08-15 }}</ref>

He was trustee of various schools, colleges and hospitals run by Walchand group.<ref>[http://www.hndpune.com/about HND Pune » About Us<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120101163230/http://www.hndpune.com/about |date=2012-01-01 }}</ref>

He was awarded with the [[Padma Shri]] award by the [[Government of India]] in 1992 for his contributions to trade and industry.<ref name=a/>

Lalchand Hirachand Doshi (24 October 1904 – 1993)  was a scion of Walchand group, noted industrialist, philanthropist and Jain social leader.
He was the youngest son of Hirachand Doshi from his second marriage and was half-brother of Walchand Hirachand, who was born from first marriage of his father. He was born in Solapur Maharashtra into a Jain family. Name of his other brothers were Gulabchand Hirachand and Ratanchand Hirachand.
He completed his Bachelor of Arts degree from Deccan College, Pune. He was admitted to the Middle Temple in London on 12 November 1926, but withdrew without being Called to the Bar on 8 November 1928. He married Lalitabai in June 1931, with whom he had three sons and a daughter.
When he grew up he joined his brother, Walchand and served its various group companies including The Scindia Steam Navigation Company Ltd., Walchandnagar Industries, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, Ravalgaon Sugar, Hindustan Construction Company, and Premier Automobiles Limited. He later served also as president of the Indian Merchants' Chamber and various other merchant bodies.
He also served as president of All India Digamber Jain Tirthakshetra Committee from 1972 to 1983, and was connected to a number of charitable institutions. He is also the author an acclaimed  book on Ramayana named as The Indian epic – Ramayana.
He was elected as an independent candidate as member of the Bombay Legislative Council, in 1939.  After India's independence, he also became a member of the Rajya Sabha from 1952 to 1958.
He was elected as the president of the Mechanical Engineers Association (India), Bombay for 1964–65 Session.
A sports aficionado, he was a member of the Cricket Club of India, the Willingdon Sports Club and various similar institutions. In addition, he was an avid golfer. He won the Dunlop Trophy for Golf and enjoyed playing tennis, badminton and bridge. He held a commercial pilot's license.
He died in October, 1993. Walchandnagar Industries is now run his sons Vinod Doshi, Chakor L. Doshi and others, whereas other companies went to sons of Gulabchand Hirachand, after family division of businesses, as the founder of the group Walchand Hirachand died without any male heirs.
He was trustee of various schools, colleges and hospitals run by Walchand group.
He was awarded with the Padma Shri award by the Government of India in 1992 for his contributions to trade and industry.
